name: Mars Pathfinder
intro: Mars Pathfinder bounced onto Mars inside giant airbags on 4 July 1997, then opened like a flower to let out Sojourner, the first Mars rover. It worked almost three times longer than planned. Renamed the Carl Sagan Memorial Station, it still rests in the old flood channel of Ares Vallis.
whyLeft: It was a one-way trip to test a cheap new way of landing. Its last signal came on 27 September 1997; engineers think its worn-out battery could no longer keep its electronics warm through the freezing nights.
repurpose: Today radioisotope heaters keep many spacecraft warm. A fresh battery and a heater blanket might let it be called again, but its 1990s electronics may have cracked in the cold.

hotspots.title: Giant airbags
hotspots.text: Pathfinder hit the ground wrapped in airbags and bounced across Mars like a huge beach ball before rolling to a stop. Then the bags were deflated and pulled in, and they still lie crumpled around the lander.

hotspots.title: Solar petals
hotspots.text: After landing, three side panels folded down like the petals of a flower. They set the lander upright and held the solar cells that powered it.

photo.alt: Folded rover on an open lander petal, surrounded by crumpled airbags, on rocky red ground.
photo.caption: Pathfinder’s first colour view: Sojourner still sits folded on an open petal, with the deflated airbags all around.

hotspots.title: The camera mast
hotspots.text: The lander’s camera sat on top of this mast. It sent home more than 16,500 pictures, including many of Sojourner at work.

hotspots.title: Weather mast
hotspots.text: This mast measured the temperature and wind, with little wind socks to show which way the breeze blew. Pathfinder sent daily weather reports from Mars.

hotspots.title: The rover ramp
hotspots.text: Sojourner drove down a ramp like this one onto the ground, a couple of days after landing. A scout would find its tracks long gone, but the rover itself should still be within about 12 meters.

hotspots.title: The battery
hotspots.text: Inside the lander’s base is a rechargeable battery. Engineers think it wore out, so the electronics froze each night. The last message arrived on 27 September 1997.

funFact: Pathfinder was renamed the Carl Sagan Memorial Station, to honour the astronomer who helped people everywhere fall in love with planets.
